description: Original evaluation set authored for EcoCompute AI. 7 categories x 7 cases. Every case has an objective, deterministic check. Split: 'calib' cases may be used to warm-start routing evidence; 'test' cases are held out and used for headline comparisons.
license: MIT (same as repository). All texts are synthetic and written for this project; no third-party data.

cases.task:
Extract the invoice number, total amount due (as a number), and due date (YYYY-MM-DD) from this text. Return JSON with keys invoice_number, total, due_date.

Text: "Thanks for your business! Invoice INV-20931 covers March services. Subtotal $1,180.00, tax $94.40, amount due $1,274.40. Payment is due on April 15, 2026."

From the email below, extract the meeting date (YYYY-MM-DD), start time (24h HH:MM), and room. Return JSON with keys date, start_time, room.

Email: "Hi team — moving our planning sync to Thursday, 2026-11-05. We'll start at 2:30 PM sharp in Room B-214 instead of the usual space. Bring Q4 numbers."

List every email address in the text, in order of first appearance, without duplicates. Return JSON: {"emails": [...]}.

Text: "Contact sales@verdant.io for quotes. Support is at help@verdant.io; escalations go to ops.lead@verdant.io. For press, write sales@verdant.io again or media-team@pressroom.org."

Extract the contact's full name, company, and phone number (digits and dashes only, as written). Return JSON with keys name, company, phone.

Text: "Following up after the expo: you spoke with Dr. Priya Raman, head of field ops at Coral Grid Systems. She asked that you call her direct line, 561-555-0147, before Friday."

Extract tracking number, carrier, and package weight in kilograms (number). Return JSON with keys tracking_number, carrier, weight_kg.

Notice: "Your order has shipped with Northwind Freight. Package 1 of 1, weight 3.4 kg, dimensions 40x30x20 cm. Tracking: NWF-88K2-5531. Estimated delivery in 3 business days."

From the review, extract the product name, the star rating as an integer, and whether the reviewer recommends it (boolean). Return JSON with keys product, rating, recommends.

Review: "I wanted to love the TrailLite 2 tent. Setup was quick, but the rainfly leaked twice on a mild night. Two stars from me, and I'd steer friends toward something else."

Extract the event's start and end dates in YYYY-MM-DD and the city. Return JSON with keys start_date, end_date, city.

Announcement: "The Reef Restoration Summit returns to Fort Lauderdale this spring, opening Tuesday, March 9, 2027 and wrapping up three days later on Thursday, March 11, 2027."

Summarize the passage in at most 40 words.

Passage: The city of Marlow Bay replaced 1,200 sodium streetlights with LED fixtures in 2025. The project cost $2.1 million and was funded by a state efficiency grant. In its first year, street-lighting electricity use fell by 58 percent, and maintenance calls dropped by half because LEDs fail less often. Residents in two neighborhoods complained about glare, so the city added shields to 140 fixtures.

Summarize the following in exactly 3 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Text: Our Q3 customer survey received 842 responses. Satisfaction rose to 4.3 out of 5, up from 4.0 last quarter. The most requested feature was offline mode, cited by 37 percent of respondents. Complaints about billing fell sharply after the September invoice redesign. Response time for support tickets remains the top pain point among enterprise customers.

Write a one-sentence summary (at most 30 words) of this incident report.

Report: At 02:14 UTC a misconfigured load balancer rule sent all European traffic to a single region. Latency rose above 4 seconds for 38 minutes. The on-call engineer rolled back the rule at 02:52. No data was lost. A config-validation check will be added to the deploy pipeline.

Summarize for a busy executive in at most 50 words. Mention the decision needed.

Memo: The warehouse in Doral is at 94 percent capacity and will run out of space by February at current growth. Option one is leasing an overflow site in Medley for $38,000 per month. Option two is adding mezzanine racking in Doral for a one-time cost of $410,000, which takes 10 weeks. Operations recommends the mezzanine because it pays back in under 11 months. A decision is needed by November 20 to finish before peak season.

Give a TL;DR in at most 25 words.

Article: Researchers tagged 46 juvenile loggerhead turtles off Palm Beach County and tracked them for 14 months. Most turtles stayed within 30 kilometers of the coast during winter, contradicting the belief that juveniles move offshore to the Gulf Stream. The team says nearshore habitat protection matters more than previously thought.

Summarize in exactly 2 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Release notes: Version 3.2 adds single sign-on through SAML and OIDC. CSV exports are now up to 5x faster for tables over 100,000 rows. The legacy v1 API will be removed on January 31; clients must migrate to v2. Dark mode received contrast fixes.

Summarize the dispute and the outcome in at most 35 words.

Case note: A tenant withheld two months of rent, arguing the landlord ignored a broken air conditioner for six weeks during summer. The housing board found the landlord in breach of the repair duty but ruled the tenant should have used the escrow process. The tenant must pay the rent; the landlord must refund one month as compensation.

tests: is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama') == True

Write a Python function merge_intervals(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]] that merges overlapping or touching closed intervals and returns them sorted by start. Example: [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10]] -> [[1,6],[8,10]]. No imports.
Write a Python function roman_to_int(s: str) -> int converting a valid Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M with subtractive notation) to an integer. No imports.
Write a Python function is_balanced(s: str) -> bool that returns True if every (, [, { in s is closed by the matching bracket in the correct order. Other characters are ignored. No imports.
Write a Python function flatten(nested: list) -> list that flattens arbitrarily nested lists into a single list, preserving order. Non-list elements are kept as-is. No imports.
Write a Python function second_largest_unique(nums: list[int]) -> int | None that returns the second-largest distinct value, or None if there are fewer than two distinct values. No imports.
